results.fact: whether approach beta for this boulder exists
results.correct_value: Approach is the North Fork Sauk River trail (standard southern Glacier Peak approach) toward White Pass and the White Chuck Glacier basin; boulder sits west of the White Chuck Glacier remnant, flat-topped, visible from the path, room for one tent at its base.
results.evidence: The route's own catalog page describes the approach as the standard North Fork Sauk River approach used for Glacier Peak (about 8 miles), with the boulder west of what remains of the White Chuck Glacier, visible from the trail, distinct flat top, and a small tent spot at its base - matching timing, itinerary.totalNote, partner_requirements, pro_tips and the stored waypoint coordinate (identical to that page's coordinate). The trail agency and a hiking database confirm the North Fork Sauk trail reaches the PCT at 8.4 mi and White Pass at ~9.1 mi, and the Gerdine/Cool route page places the White Chuck basin east of White Pass. The approach field's claim that no beta exists is a stale refusal. New text avoids a mileage figure since the boulder lies somewhat beyond White Pass.

results.evidence: The Gerdine Ridge/Cool Glacier and Disappointment Peak Cleaver route pages both start the route from White Pass on the PCT via the North Fork Sauk trail and Glacier Gap. A guide service's 4-day itinerary: Sloan Creek trailhead 2,100 ft, day 1 to White Pass camp 5,900 ft, day 2 to Glacier Gap 7,300 ft (+1,400 ft), day 3 summit and back, day 4 out; another guide itinerary and a single-day trip report use the same North Fork Sauk/White Pass/Glacier Gap line. The trail agency puts the PCT at 8.4 mi and White Pass ~0.75 mi beyond; a hiking database gives the trailhead at 48.0584,-121.2866, so the stored waypoint[0] pin IS the North Fork Sauk trailhead and its note calling it the Trinity trailhead is false. The Buck Creek Pass/Trinity itinerary text was contamination; per-day gains now use net elevations (2,100 -> 5,900 -> 7,300 -> 10,541). results.fact: total elevation gain for the trip
results.evidence: The 7,750 ft itinerary total belonged to the contaminated Buck Creek Pass itinerary; the corrected itinerary days now sum to the net 8,450 ft (trailhead ~2,100 to summit 10,541). Published totals for the North Fork Sauk route disagree: one guide says ~9,000 ft, another 9,200 ft, a single-day trip report 12,000 ft; the row's own corrections note says its figure is a computed net. None supports 9,846 exactly and the undulation through the White Chuck basin is not quantified, so gain_ft/loss_ft are left unchanged and the totalNote no longer states a gain number. gain_ft (9,846) and the itinerary TOTAL (8,450) still differ and need a decision.

dist_km (7.7 mi) is the one-way approach and the 25 mi itinerary is a round trip, so those two do not conflict; day 1 of the itinerary is 8 mi. The real disagreement is inside the row: approach prose (4 + 1.7 + 2 mi = 7.7 mi to Glacier Creek) vs the waypoints (Kennedy Ridge junction at 6 mi, Glacier Creek camp at 9.7 mi). One route description gives 'about 4 miles' on the White Chuck trail; a Frostbite Ridge trip report gives 'approximately 6 miles'; a 1975 report implies ~5 mi to Kennedy. With the road also closed short of the trailhead, the one-way figure cannot be settled by two agreeing sources, so no patch.
